paper_metadata.title: 40-GHz Transimpedance Amplifier With Differential Outputs Using InP–InGaAs Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors
paper_metadata.abstract: High-gain and high-bandwidth transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs) are required for fiber-optic receiver modules. This paper reports on the design, fabrication, and characterization of a 40-Gb/s TIA for SONET/SDH STS-768/STM-256 applications based on an InP–InGaAs single heterojunction bipolar transistor Fig. 1. Block diagram of a typical 40 Gb/s optical receiver module. PA: (SHBT) process developed at Vitesse Semiconductor Corporation post-amplifier. (Vitesse Indium Phosphide Release 1 or VIP-1). This amplifier consists of a single-ended input transimpedance pre-amplifier and a differential output post-amplifier. The measured differential transimpedance is 1800 with 3-dB bandwidth greater than 40 GHz. The high gain of this circuit eliminates the need for a standalone limiting amplifier between the conventional transimpedance preamplifier and the demultiplexer in short-reach applications.
